kindled seizures induce a chronic increase in vasopression mRNA in the supraoptic neurons of the rat hypothalamus.
kindled seizures induce a persistent increase in vasoppressin mRNA in the hypothalamus of rats.
kindling seizures induce a long term increase in vasopression mRNA in magnocellular neurons of the hypothalamic supraoptic nucleus.

the neurochemical and neuroendocrine changes that accompany epilepsy.
the role of neuroendocrine factors in epilepsy.
the neuroendocrine changes associated with seizures and epilepsy.

the increase in vasopression mRNA after kindling is a long-term effect of the seizure that persists in the absence of further seizure activity and is not dependent on the maintenance of body fluid homeostatis.

the kindling-induced increase in VP mRNA expression in the hypothalmoic supraoptic nucleus is long-lasting, is independent of seizures, and may be a mechanism for the neuroendocrine disturbance associated with epilepsy.
kindled seizures can cause long term changes in gene expression that may have important implications for understanding the neuroendocrine and other disturbances associated with epilepsy.

kindled seizures induce long term increase in vasopression mRNA in the supraoptic nuclei of the hypothalamus, and the change in vasopression expression is independent of the number of kindled stimuli or the number of seizures, and is correlated with the duration afterdischarge.
